课程简介（中文）

本课程不仅介绍生育、死亡、人口增长等人口事件，还探讨人口变化与社会经济转型之间的联系。我们提出一系列问题：生育率和死亡率下降的根源是什么？人口老龄化对中国社会发展带来怎样机遇和挑战？户籍制度的最新改革将如何影响人口流动？中国年轻人的婚姻观念有怎样的改变？对这些问题的探究，可以帮助学生更深入地理解当代人口转型与社会变迁。

课程简介（英文）

This course introduces key demographic events like fertility, mortality, and population growth, while exploring the links between population change and socio-economic transformation. We examine critical questions: What drives declining fertility and mortality? What opportunities and challenges does an aging society present? How will recent reforms to the hukou system affect migration? And how are young people’s views on marriage evolving? Exploring these issues offers students a deeper understanding of contemporary demographic transitions and social change.

教学目标

Through an in-depth analysis of China’s unique demographic trajectory, transitional process, policy logic, achievements, and challenges, this course aims to help students develop a scientific and objective understanding of China’s fundamental national conditions and social governance, while fostering a rational appreciation of China’s development path and its institutional strengths.

The course integrates insights from demography, economics, sociology, and public policy, emphasizing the use of theoretical frameworks and empirical data to analyze real-world issues. Grounded in the principle of linking theory with practice, the course guides students to identify critical issues and emerging challenges in China’s population and development landscape. Through research-oriented learning modules, it seeks to ignite academic curiosity, cultivate foundational awareness of academic norms and research skills, and equip students pursuing advanced studies or careers in policy analysis and international organizations.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

教学方式

The course combines lectures by the instructor with student presentations and discussions. Starting from the second week, following the instructor's lecture, one student will deliver a 15-minute presentation on a topic assigned from the syllabus. For the term paper, students are required to select a topic related to demographic and socioeconomic transformation. At the end of the semester, students will have the opportunity to present their term paper findings. The paper should be approximately 3,000 words in English and follow the structure of an academic research paper, including an introduction, literature review, analysis, and conclusion.

 

 

 

教学内容与进度安排

 

Week 1 (March 27) Introduction to Demography and Chinese Population

Peng, X. 2011. China’s demographic history and future challenges. Science, 333(6042), 581-587.

Gu, D., Andreev, K., Dupre, M.E. 2021. Major trends in population growth around the world. China CDC weekly, 3(28): 604.

 

Week 2-3 (April 3, 10) Fertility Measures and Fertility Transitions

Cai, Y. 2010. China’s Below Replacement Fertility: Government Policy or Socioeconomic Development. Population and Development Review, 36(3): 419-440.

Zhang, J. 2017. The evolution of China’s one-child policy and its effects on family outcomes. Journal of Economic Perspectives, 31(1), 141-160.

Week 2 Assignment

Student presentation: discuss the effectiveness of different kinds of pro-natal policies

Week 3 Assignment

Student presentation: discuss the pros and cons of being a single child

 

Week 4 (April 17) Evolution of Fertility Policies and Policy Implications

Gu, B., Wang, F., Guo, Z. and Zhang, E. 2007. China's Local and National Fertility Policies at the End of the Twentieth Century. Population and Development Review, 33(1): 129-147.

Shen, K., Wang, F. and Cai, C. 2020. Government policy and global fertility change: a reappraisal. Asian Population Studies, 16(2), 145-166.

Week 4 Assignment

Student presentation: discuss how to promote father’s involvement in childcare

 

Week 5, 7 (April 24, May 8) Mortality Transition and Health Care Reform

Chen, H., Qian, Y., Dong, Y., & et al. 2020. Patterns and changes in life expectancy in China, 1990-2016. PLoS One, 15(4), e0231007.

Yip, W., Fu, H. and et al. 2021. 10 years of health-care reform in China: progress and gaps in Universal Health Coverage. Lancet, 394: 1192–204

Week 5 Assignment

Student presentation: introduce the health care system in a developed country

Week 7 Assignment

Student presentation: discuss the potential challenges associated with integrating new technologies into health care systems

 

Week 6 (May 1) No class, Labour Day

 

Week 8 (May 15) No class, Sports Meeting

 

Week 9 (May 22) Demographic Transition and Demographic Dividend

Mason, A., Lee, R., & NTA Network. 2022. Six ways population change will affect the global economy. Population and development review, 48(1), 51-73.

*Cai, F. 2020. The second demographic dividend as a driver of China's growth. China & World Economy, 28(5), 26-44.

Week 9 Assignment

Student presentation: Introduce the policies aimed at reducing youth unemployment in any country except China.

 

Week 10 (May 29) Population Aging and Social Security System

Cheng, L., Liu, H., Zhang, Y. and Zhao, Z. 2018. The heterogeneous impact of pension income on elderly living arrangements: Evidence from China’s New Rural Pension Scheme. Journal of Population Economics, 31(1): 155–192.

Cai, Y., Wang, F., and Shen, K. 2018. Fiscal implications of population aging and welfare expansion in China. Population and Development Review, 44(4), 811-831.

Week 10 Assignment

Student presentation: Introduce the long-term care insurance in a country

 

Week 11 (June 5) Student Presentations (For 2-credit students)

 

Week 12 (June 12) Migration, Urbanization and Hukou Reform

Chan, K.W. 2019. Two systems in one country: the origin, functions, and mechanisms of the rural-urban dual system in China. Eurasian Geography and Economics, 60(4): 422-454.

Chen, M., Liu, W., Lu, D., Chen, H., & Ye, C. 2018. Progress of China's new-type urbanization construction since 2014: A preliminary assessment. Cities, 78, 180-193.

Week 12 Assignment

Student presentation: Introduce the policies to attract talents in a country

 

Week 13 (June 19) Social Change and Marriage Institution

Guilmoto, C.Z. 2012. Skewed Sex Ratios at Birth and Future Marriage Squeeze in China and India, 2005–2100. Demography, 49, 77-100.

Desai, S., Chen, F., Reddy, S., & McLaughlin, A. 2022. Measuring Women's Empowerment in the Global South. Annual Review of Sociology, 48, 507-527.

Week 13 Assignment

Student presentation: discuss whether pre-marital cohabitation is beneficial for marital stability

 

Week 14 (June 26) Student Presentations for 3-credit students and Final Essay of all students
